approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using accepted task-local scores. It keeps a bounded score-ranked breeding population, draws parents from high-scoring rank bands, and produces either connected-fragment crossovers with optional finishing mutation or ordinary mutation walks. Ordinary walks usually make one edit call and sometimes two or three; obstruction can force longer walks. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. At each suggestion the Parent fits its count-fingerprint Gaussian process to the complete accepted archive, generates a fresh surplus pool containing only final products, and uses correlated posterior draws to choose the announced evaluation batch. Real accepted scores then update both breeding survivors and the next model fit. The model is already fitted when a mutation walk starts, but does not guide its intermediate steps.
approach.novelty: Add two-arm posterior-mean guidance to optional ordinary continuation. After the unchanged first mutation, each requested second or third step at the ordinary saturation floor tries two fresh mutations from the same current intermediate and continues with the higher predicted raw score. Only the chosen path's final product can enter the original pool. Earlier siblings removed continuation, admitted intermediate products into finite pool slots, or changed predictive fitting and final allocation. This variant preserves the continuation schedule, independent final-product slots and correlated final selector while changing one decision inside the walk. It tests whether an existing useful predictor can guide the next graph step; a predicted arm advantage is evidence of that decision, not measured score improvement.

hypothesis: Modify optional ordinary second/third mutation continuation at saturation floor one by drawing exactly two fresh arms from the same current intermediate and continuing with the valid arm of greatest raw-score posterior mean from the existing suggestion-entry accepted-label count GP, with first-arm exact ties and bounded inherited fallbacks, while retaining the full final-product pool and correlated final selector.

finding_summary.headline: Two-arm choices reached evaluation and later breeding, but mean Top-1 fell by 0.048083
finding_summary.insights: This result rules out lack of execution, absent evaluated delivery, lost feedback, zero cohort-level recursion and reduced final-pool capacity as explanations for the failure of this fixed rule. The model successfully imposed its preferences without producing better search. Across all accepted offspring, mean raw score fell from 0.385256 to 0.326704 while mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.395280. Parent-beating counts rose from 629 to 690 and incumbent-update counts from 258 to 261, yet total incumbent increments fell from 5.807663 to 5.086425. More local wins therefore coexist with weaker sources and less endpoint progress. Selected-stream prediction MSE fell from 0.012718 to 0.007832, but the labels being predicted changed and recorded 1.96-standard-deviation coverage fell from 76.28% to 74.60%; this does not establish better transferable calibration. Chemistry inspection likewise finds both recognizable aromatic amides and amines and persistent questionable bond environments, ring geometries and unresolved stereochemistry. The largest deficits include failure to reproduce a compact high-scoring heterocyclic combination, but neither missing rings/amines nor a specific chemical mediator is established. Most unchosen arms remain unscored, and no alternate continuation future was executed. The evidence supports a negative total contribution of this exact fixed guidance rule under these conditions; it leaves the separate roles of local prediction preferences, extra random draws and later adaptive history unresolved, and does not reverse the value of ordinary continuation itself.
finding_summary.results: The continuation rule executed 8,640 two-arm decisions. Independently reconstructed predictions confirm 4,266 strict choices of a different second-arm identity; 44 exact ties chose the first arm. Those changed paths delivered 237 distinct evaluated finals. All 230 with another suggestion remaining entered the next model fit, and 120 later served as breeding parents. The audit also retains 110 nonterminal finals with no later use and seven terminal births; one task/seed had six affected accepted finals and no later breeding. Final proposal capacity stayed at 160 products per suggestion. Nevertheless, mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.547587, a paired change of -0.048083 against the required +0.002. All three seed macros and all five task means decreased; four of the 15 individual task/seed cells improved. Macro population SD declined from 0.026593 to 0.017941, but the gain criterion failed.

molecular.headline: Aromatic amides and aryl amines coexist with enlarged heterocycles, reactive bonds and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-87c89dda7e3b produces substituted indole amides, azaaromatic methylamines, compressed ring systems, linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione assemblies, flexible and cyclic aryl amines, medium-ring lactams and fluorinated imino/dione heterocycles. Ordinary medicinal-chemistry groups are present, but many outputs also contain unusual heteroatom bonds, large repeated assemblies or unresolved ring geometry. Some leaders are appreciably more conventional than their close high-scoring relatives; neither universal implausibility nor a general absence of rings, amines or heterocycles fits the evidence. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, with recurring leading families within individual streams. The weak drug-likeness judgement concerns the mixed output and its liabilities, not a claim that every compound is unsuitable. No synthesis, stability, protonation, conformation or biological activity has been established by this inspection. The digest was read before all 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory files. All paths exist; all 9,000 records were read, covering every task and Search Seed 0, 1 and 2. Each task has 900 Child records, including 870 evaluated optimizer proposals. There are no tasks without trajectories. The immutable comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile mismatch. This is therefore a complete descriptive chemistry comparison with n-62daf219c70a, not an absent or partial Parent comparison. The profile is the supplied Research in Depth profile, 300 observations per task and feedback batch size 10, with direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled. The Parent source of record is runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-62daf219c70a/seed-{0,1,2}/trajectories; its full Molecular report and the original n-c55c3d520a2c gap report were read through the supplied evidence index. Current gaps retain that historical provenance while describing changed current molecules. In fixed task order, digest ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9655, 0.9747, 0.9862, 0.9839 and 0.9517; aromatic-atom-string incidences are 0.9644, 0.9736, 0.9839, 0.9747 and 0.9506. These are molecule-level SMILES-text incidences, not aromatic atom fractions or ring counts. Every task has charged-string and stereocentre-string incidence 0.0. Neutral strings nevertheless contain readily recognizable ionizable amines. Independent RDKit readings of evaluated optimizer molecules give median heavy-atom counts 25, 43, 33, 32 and 27; no optimizer row failed parsing. Parsing does not certify chemical feasibility. All counts and molecule descriptors below derive from these supplied trajectories; the audit and annotated row provenance are in .slots/round-0024-slot-1/molecular_chemistry_audit_slot1.json and molecular_annotated_trajectories_slot1.jsonl. Scores are the recorded labels, never recomputed. Last emissions are distinguished from retained best molecules. Unchosen continuation arms have no labels here and receive no chemical outcome credit. Changed chemical families, alert counts or high-score associations do not identify activation, component contribution, mediation, or the cause of any endpoint difference.

per_task.generated_character: Evaluated proposals have median 25 heavy atoms, range 1-41, and predominantly aromatic ring systems. Seed 2 reaches a 24-heavy-atom ethynyl/dimethyl/methoxy indole carboxamide attached to pyridine: a recognizable three-ring heteroaryl amide without a halogen or sulfur triple bond. Seed 0 instead reaches a 25-heavy-atom dimethoxy azaaromatic bicyclic region joined through methylene and an N-chloro or N-bromo aniline nitrogen to a fluorophenyl ring; this leading family has no carbonyl. Seed 1 reaches a 24-heavy-atom oxygenated, tightly connected ring framework carrying an imine, a ketone and an amino/pyridyl side chain; RDKit perceives four-membered closures and an unassigned centre. The stream can therefore make conventional aromatic amides, but it also explores strained connectivities and carbon-sulfur triple-bond strings. Such sulfur bonds occur in 95 of 870 Child optimizer rows versus none of the matched Parent rows for this task. N-halogen bonds occur in 314 Child rows versus 445 Parent rows, so one liability declines while another appears.
liabilities: N-Cl and N-Br substitution occurs on amine or amide nitrogen in strong examples; the carbon-sulfur triple-bond strings are particularly unusual synthetic targets.
Dense small-ring connectivity in seed 1 and its unspecified stereochemical centre leave geometry and molecular identity unresolved.
Tiny floor-scoring molecules are still evaluated late, including the seed-0 NCl and seed-1 oxetane at evaluation 286.
missing_features: Consistent conventional bond environments around the favorable compact aromatic/polar arrangement are missing across the emitted set, although the leading seed-2 indole amide is an explicit counterexample to universal chemical implausibility.
Independent feasible replacements for the compressed seed-1 topology are not demonstrated at its leading score; a ring-rich string alone does not establish a geometrically accessible scaffold.

The observed scores do not identify a unique absent target pharmacophore. Amide, carbonyl-free azaaromatic and constrained families all score above the initial best, so no single functional group can be prescribed from this panel.

Seed 1 reaches a 62-heavy-atom repeated fused nitrogen-dione assembly; nearby examples use peroxide linkages and N-halogen bonds. These are rich ring graphs, but their repeated units, numerous heteroatoms and reactive attachments make straightforward synthesis and ordinary drug-like size doubtful.
liabilities: Oversized repeated heterocycles carry many carbonyl and heteroatom groups while giving only modest changes within the observed score band.
Strong examples include peroxides, N-halogen bonds, haloalkyl esters, chloromethyl groups and cumulene chains; these raise environment-specific reactivity and synthesis concerns.

Aromatic notation on a nine-membered heterocycle does not establish an accessible planar aromatic state. The near-tied smaller fused-ring relative shows that this unusual topology is not universally required.
missing_features: Compact alternatives retaining the favorable linked nitrogen/carbonyl/thione organization are not consistently delivered at the stronger Parent score. Compactness is already possible in the Child and is not itself a demonstrated causal remedy.
Conventional, synthetically credible substitutes for the repeated peroxide/N-halogen assemblies and haloalkynyl appendages are not established at their recorded scores.

The larger aromatic-labelled ring lacks demonstrated conformational and tautomeric identity; no exact missing objective-specific arrangement can be inferred solely from the Parent/Child family difference.

The seed-0 leader is a relatively conventional 25-heavy-atom molecule with two alkyl-linked phenyl rings, two primary amines, two phenols and carbon-bound fluorine. liabilities: The seed-1 hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur environment, small nitrogen rings and chloromethyl group warrant chemical scrutiny; representability is not proof of an ordinary stable sulfur functional group.
Flexible multiply aminated chains, phenols, thioethers and occasional N-O or O-Cl substituents leave stability, oxidation and solution-state behaviour unresolved.
The neutral SMILES omit stereochemical assignments even where the parsed structures contain potential centres; neutral notation does not mean the amines are nonionizable.
missing_features: The missing capability is reliable presentation of the already present aromatic/available-amine organization in conventional, resolved structures; neither basic nitrogen nor saturated nitrogen rings are absent.

Specified stereochemical identity is absent for the branched chains, fluorinated centres and substituted nitrogen rings. Actual protonation and conformational preferences are unmeasured by this audit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: the gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and retained by the identical-trajectory baseline n-62daf219c70a; it is re-observed in changed outputs of n-87c89dda7e3b on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 under the supplied 300-observation, batch-10 profile with direct aromatic C/N exchange disabled. Strong emitted examples include N-halogen bonds, peroxide links, an imidoyl fluoride, an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur environment and carbon-sulfur triple-bond strings. One current aromatic-amide stream has 95 sulfur-triple-bond outputs versus none in its matched Parent stream, yet its best molecule contains an ordinary terminal alkyne instead. Conventional indole amides, primary arylalkyl amines and saturated diamine rings are counterexamples to a universal inability to generate plausible groups.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments while retaining otherwise useful aromatic and polar structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need awareness of the bonding environment and the ability to offer conventional alternatives while preserving combinations supported by local accepted feedback. Ordinary carbon-bound halogens and useful amines must remain distinguishable from unusual heteroatom bonds. These observations justify a chemical capability gap, not a universal filter, a guaranteed score gain, or attribution to the current continuation decision.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction and scaffold changes need ring-size, bridge-connectivity and unsaturation awareness, together with feasible alternative connectivities that retain learned functional relationships. Aromatic labels and ring counts cannot supply that information. This is not a ban on small or medium rings, nor evidence that geometric scrutiny would itself improve the recorded objective.

Protonation, tautomerism and conformational identity are separate questions. This evidence establishes unspecified chemical identity, not a measured stereochemical score penalty or a missing basic-amine capability.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Proposals need feedback-informed ways to preserve functional-group relationships while simplifying, replacing or expanding dispensable portions. The capability gap is consistent context control, not an inability to add atoms or form rings. A fixed minimum size, automatic growth preference or universal fragmentation prohibition does not follow, and the observed molecule associations do not identify which retained component produced them.

Strong excerpts repeatedly alter short chains, halogen placement, ether length, local nitrogen sites or ring segments within retained aromatic-amide, linked heterocycle, aryl-amine, macrocyclic-lactam and fluorinated-dione families. The Child and Parent do show different families across seeds, including conventional counterexamples, so global structural collapse is not supported. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Scaffold-level proposals need to reorganize locally supported functional relationships into chemically independent, credible connectivities. Actual accepted labels and chemical plausibility must distinguish useful alternatives from merely distinct graph strings. This conditional coverage gap neither identifies a target-specific scaffold nor proves that more diversity, or any particular search component, would improve the endpoint.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using accepted task-local scores. It keeps a bounded score-ranked breeding population, draws parents from high-scoring rank bands, and produces either connected-fragment crossovers with optional finishing mutation or ordinary mutation walks. Ordinary walks usually make one edit call and sometimes two or three; obstruction can force longer walks. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. At each suggestion the Parent fits its count-fingerprint Gaussian process to the complete accepted archive, generates a fresh surplus pool containing only final products, and uses correlated posterior draws to choose the announced evaluation batch. Real accepted scores then update both breeding survivors and the next model fit. The model is already fitted when a mutation walk starts, but does not guide its intermediate steps.

Earlier siblings removed continuation, admitted intermediate products into finite pool slots, or changed predictive fitting and final allocation. This variant preserves the continuation schedule, independent final-product slots and correlated final selector while changing one decision inside the walk. It tests whether an existing useful predictor can guide the next graph step; a predicted arm advantage is evidence of that decision, not measured score improvement.

Parent-beating counts rose from 629 to 690 and incumbent-update counts from 258 to 261, yet total incumbent increments fell from 5.807663 to 5.086425. Selected-stream prediction MSE fell from 0.012718 to 0.007832, but the labels being predicted changed and recorded 1.96-standard-deviation coverage fell from 76.28% to 74.60%; this does not establish better transferable calibration. Chemistry inspection likewise finds both recognizable aromatic amides and amines and persistent questionable bond environments, ring geometries and unresolved stereochemistry. The largest deficits include failure to reproduce a compact high-scoring heterocyclic combination, but neither missing rings/amines nor a specific chemical mediator is established. Most unchosen arms remain unscored, and no alternate continuation future was executed. The evidence supports a negative total contribution of this exact fixed guidance rule under these conditions; it leaves the separate roles of local prediction preferences, extra random draws and later adaptive history unresolved, and does not reverse the value of ordinary continuation itself.
